title: Rules of Appeal Procedure, Annotated — Hearing Setting and Notice (Unemployment Insurance Appeals)
content:
Clause by clause, with the superseded clauses marked, the rule of Unemployment Insurance Appeals on hearing setting and notice reads:

**(a)** Dockets with hearings are set for a hearing in the docket's default mode, and a party may ask for an in-person hearing where the docket allows it; the Board of Review decides on the record and sets no hearing, accepting written argument within its written argument days.

> *Annotation:* Clause (a) is **no longer in force** as worded. It has been superseded by the current basis on hearing modes.

**(b)** A hearing is set only while the appeal status is filed, scheduled or dismissed.

**(c)** The first hearing is set within the docket's scheduling target after filing, the hearing notice is mailed at least the notice minimum days before the hearing date, and every interested party of the docket is notified.

> *Annotation:* Clause (c) is **no longer in force** as worded. It has been superseded by the current basis for setting the first hearing.

**(d)** Each party must register the phone number at which it will be called no later than the registration business days before the hearing; the hearing officer calls at the start time and waits the call wait minutes before proceeding without a party who does not answer.

**(e)** Hearing notices and decisions are delivered by mail and in the online portal.

## Commentary on clause (b): the status condition

Whether a hearing may be set is read from the appeal's status on the Department's record of that appeal at the time of setting. The clause is exhaustive ("only while"):

| Status of the appeal | A hearing may be set |
|---|---|
| filed | yes |
| scheduled | yes |
| dismissed | yes |
| decided | no |
| withdrawn | no |
| closed | no |

Each setting is recorded on the appeal's activity with the hearing date, the start time, the mode, the date the notice was mailed and the reason for the setting: the first setting, a reset after a granted postponement, or a setting after reopening.

## Commentary on clause (d): the telephone hearing

- The registration deadline is counted in business days before the hearing date and fixed per docket; a number registered later than that deadline does not meet the clause.
- At the start time the hearing officer calls each party at its registered number. A party that has not answered when the call wait minutes have run is proceeded without.

*Illustration (hypothetical):* with a call wait of 15 minutes and a 09:00 start, a party that answers at 09:10 takes part; a party that has still not answered at 09:15 is proceeded without.

superseded_clauses: Dockets with hearings are set for a hearing in the docket's default mode, and a party may ask for an in-person hearing where the docket allows it; the Board of Review decides on the record and sets no hearing, accepting written argument within its written argument days.

The first hearing is set within the docket's scheduling target after filing, the hearing notice is mailed at least the notice minimum days before the hearing date, and every interested party of the docket is notified.
